text.content:
Family, honor, Heywood. The last cartel network standing.

Turf: Heywood: Vista del Rey, the Glen's old Reclamation Zone blocks and south Wellsprings; pushing into Arroyo
Known for: Ground cars, handguns and street drugs; a strict code; funerals, food and a little justice
Leadership: "Don" Campo Orta
Allies & rivals: At war with 6th Street. Patrons of Las Calaveritas and the Princesses of Justice
Hangouts: El Coyote Cojo (#32), La Catrina (#39), Mercado Sonora (#40)

The Valentinos are what's left of every Mexican and South American cartel that ever worked Night City. The Purge drove the cartels underground in 2047; the bloodbath of Moto Cielo in 2058 put the Valentinos on top of them. After that you joined, you died, or you got out of the life.

They are bound to their community by blood and by a strict code drawn from their culture: protect the people who grew up here, honor the dead, and never sell to children. Break it and the Valentinos handle you, not the cops. Relatives run bars, corner shops, clubs and garages, and those businesses front the gang's money. Gold, saints, Santa Muerte, beautiful old cars and good manners.

In Vista del Rey they do what the city won't: they bury the dead, feed the living, and pay for the night shift at Crisis Medical Center. In the Glen they and the NCPD have an understanding: no shootings near the courthouse. In 2070 the war with 6th Street spills in from Arroyo, and there are Valentino funerals every week; Lupe "Lady Luck" Torres commands it.

Edgerunner's Handbook p.26; Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.02, 04, 10
